method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2) 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)' (published 3 July 2024). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS <license> element for PMC11467073 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 503 on 2026-09-23)).

claims.claim: **Testicular cancer is the commonest tumour in males aged 15–39.** Suspect it with any solid, painless testicular lump; about 10% present with metastatic symptoms (back pain, leg swelling, breathlessness, cough, neck mass, gynaecomastia). Investigate at once: delay worsens stage.
claims.source_text: Testicular cancer is the most frequent tumor in adolescent and young adult males aged between 15 and 39 years … TGCT should be suspected in any male with a solid, painless testicular nodule. A history of cryptorchidism or atrophic testes may be present. Approximately 10% of patients have symptoms of metastatic disease such as lumbar back pain, lower extremity swelling, dyspnea, cough, neck mass enlargement, gynecomastia or paraneoplastic hyperthyroidism. If suspected, diagnosis should be started immediately as any delay in diagnosis may adversely affect tumor stage and prognosis
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work-up:** bilateral testicular ultrasound, bloods, tumour markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) before and after orchiectomy, and CT chest, abdomen and pelvis. Brain imaging for more than 5 lung nodules, poor IGCCCG risk or beta-hCG above 5000 mIU/ml. FDG-PET has no staging role.
claims.source_text: After a complete physical examination, bilateral high-frequency ultrasound of the testis is required to confirm the presence of a testicular mass and to examine the contralateral testis. The presence of microlithiasis as a single finding is not diagnostic. Other mandatory investigations include a complete blood count and chemistry profile, including pre- and post-orchiectomy STM such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), beta-subunit of human chorionic gonadotropin (bHCG) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and a thoraco-abdominopelvic CT scan. … Brain imaging is recommended in patients with extensive pulmonary metastases (i.e., >5 pulmonary nodules), poor IGCCCG risk, very high bHCG levels (i.e., >5000 mIU/ml) or when clinically indicated … There is no evidence to support the use of fluorodeoxyglucose PET (FDG-PET) in the staging of testicular cancer
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Radical inguinal orchiectomy is mandatory; never do a trans-scrotal biopsy or orchiectomy** (it alters lymphatic drainage). With life-threatening metastatic disease, start chemotherapy first and delay orchiectomy.
claims.source_text: Radical inguinal orchiectomy with ligation of the spermatic cord at the internal inguinal ring is mandatory to facilitate histopathological and prognostic evaluation of the primary tumor and to provide adequate oncologic control … However, in patients with elevated tumor markers and high burden or life-threatening metastatic disease requiring urgent treatment, chemotherapy may be started immediately and orchiectomy delayed until clinical stabilization. … Partial or trans-scrotal biopsy or orchiectomy, are not recommended as they alters the lymphatic drainage to inguinal nodes ("scrotal violation")
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Normal markers do not exclude a germ cell tumour.** A raised AFP rules out pure seminoma. After orchiectomy, markers should fall with their half-lives (AFP 5–7 days, beta-hCG 1–3 days); failure to fall means residual disease.
claims.source_text: However, they have low sensitivity and normal values do not exclude TGCT. … AFP is not elevated in pure seminomas where an increase of AFP indicates a non-seminoma component. … A progressive decline to normalization according to their half-lives (5-7 days for AFP and 1-3 days for bHCG) confirms that orchiectomy has removed all tumor disease, otherwise they provide early evidence of residual disease or recurrence.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer fertility counselling and sperm banking routinely before any treatment, ideally before orchiectomy.**
claims.source_text: Information and counselling on fertility issues and sperm cryopreservation should be offered routinely prior to the initiation of any form of treatment, ideally prior to orchiectomy.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage I seminoma:** active surveillance is preferred for most; a single dose of carboplatin (AUC 7) is the alternative, especially with more than one risk factor. Use para-aortic radiotherapy only if chemotherapy is contraindicated.
claims.source_text: Active surveillance is the preferred strategy for most patients, but adjuvant chemotherapy with a single course of carboplatin (area under the curve of 7) is an alternative, especially for those with more than one risk factor or for those unwilling or unable to undergo surveillance … low-dose reduced paraaortic adjuvant radiotherapy should only be recommended if chemotherapy is contraindicated
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage I non-seminoma:** orchiectomy alone cures about 75%. Lymphovascular invasion raises relapse risk to about 50%. Surveillance is excellent for all; alternatively one cycle of BEP cuts relapse below 5% in patients with lymphovascular invasion.
claims.source_text: Orchiectomy alone cures about 75% of these patients. … The presence of LVI in the primary tumor defines a subgroup with a high risk of relapse, approaching 50% … one cycle of standard BEP chemotherapy (Table 5) reduces the risk of relapse to less than 5% in patients with LVI and is the most commonly recommended adjuvant treatment for patients with LVI
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **BEP (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) is standard,** chosen by IGCCCG risk: three cycles for good risk, four for intermediate and poor risk.
claims.source_text: Bleomycin, etoposide and cisplatin (BEP) is the standard of care. Patients with intermediate- and poor-risk IGCCCG should be treated with four cycles of BEP, whereas patients with good-risk IGCCCG can be safely treated with three cycles of BEP
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bleomycin may be unsuitable** over age 40, with lung disease, heavy smoking, jobs needing high lung capacity, mediastinal tumours or planned lung surgery or radiotherapy. Check spirometry and DLCO at baseline and during treatment; stop bleomycin if DLCO falls by more than 25%.
claims.source_text: An absolute or relative contraindication to bleomycin may exist in patients over 40 years of age, those with pulmonary disease, heavy smokers, athletes or professionals who require a high lung capacity, and those with mediastinal tumors or lung metastases, especially if extensive pulmonary resection or radiation is planned after chemotherapy … Baseline and follow-up spirometry and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) may identify these patients as ineligible for bleomycin, as well as early toxicity during treatment. Bleomycin toxicity should be suspected in any patient with sudden onset of cough or dyspnea. A decrease in corrected DLCO is a predictor of bleomycin-induced pneumonitis. We recommend discontinuing bleomycin if a decrease in DLCO greater than 25% is observed
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bleomycin toxicity presents as sudden cough or breathlessness.** Adjust the dose when creatinine clearance is below 50 ml/min, and keep the total cumulative dose within 360–400 units.
claims.source_text: Bleomycin toxicity should be suspected in any patient with sudden onset of cough or dyspnea. … although the dose should be adjusted in patients with a creatinine clearance <50 ml/min and discontinued in the event of pulmonary toxicity. In any case, the total cumulative dose should not exceed 360-400 UI.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without bleomycin:** four cycles of EP for good risk; VIP with G-CSF for intermediate or poor risk. Carboplatin combinations are inferior to cisplatin ones.
claims.source_text: If there is a contraindication to bleomycin in patients with IGCCCG good prognosis tumors, four cycles of EP [] may be used as an alternative … For patients with advanced IGCCCG intermediate or poor prognosis tumors, the alternative first line schedule is VIP (Table 5) plus prophylactic G-CSF [, ]. Combinations of carboplatin with etoposide (EC) in patients with good prognosis or with bleomycin and etoposide in NSGCT (BEC) are inferior to the same combinations with cisplatin
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give full doses on time with G-CSF support;** reduced dose intensity worsens outcomes. Check markers before each cycle: an inadequate fall after one or two cycles signals poorer prognosis.
claims.source_text: The oncologist should aim to administer the full dose at the scheduled time, avoiding delays and dose reductions as much as possible, as lower dose intensity is associated with worse outcomes []. We recommend prophylactic G-CSF to achieve these goals. … Patients with inadequate decline after the first or second cycle represent a group with a poorer prognosis.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat high-risk and relapsed patients in experienced multidisciplinary centres.**
claims.source_text: patients with TGCT at high risk of recurrence, as well as those who have relapsed, be treated by multidisciplinary teams in experienced centers
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-seminoma with normal markers and residual retroperitoneal nodes of 1 cm or more: nerve-sparing RPLND** (PET is not useful). **Seminoma residuals under 3 cm: surveillance;** larger ones need PET at least 6 weeks after the last bleomycin.
claims.source_text: Patients with NSGCT, post-chemotherapy negative tumor markers and residual retroperitoneal lymph nodes ≥1 cm in larger axial diameter should undergo surgery, preferentially an open nerve-sparing retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND). In large residual masses, a full bilateral RPLND is recommended, whereas a modified template RPLND can be considered in cases of low volume before and after CT []. FDG-PET-CT is not recommended for the evaluation of residual disease in NSGCT. … active surveillance is recommended for patients with disseminated seminoma and post-chemotherapy residual disease with a larger diameter less than 3 cm. In the rest of patients, a FDG PET/CT should be done at least 6 weeks after the last dose of bleomycin.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Choriocarcinoma syndrome or high ARDS risk** (extensive lung metastases, hypoxaemia): start with a dose-reduced induction such as 2–3 day EP or baby-BOP, then full cycles once stable. Prevent tumour lysis when tumour volume is large.
claims.source_text: Because bleeding leading to ARDS and other severe complications may even be triggered with the first standard cycle of chemotherapy, an initial dose-reduced induction regimen such as a 2- or 3-day EP [, ]or baby-BOP (Cisplatin 50 mg/m2, vincristine 2 mg, and bleomycin 30 U on day 1) [] has been recommended. After 14 days of this regimen once the patient is stabilized the full number of cycles should be applied following the induction cycle. … These induction approaches are also valid for other patients with NSGCT and at high risk of ARDS due to extensive lung metastases, dyspnea or hypoxemia at diagnosis. … In cases of extensive tumor volume, prevention measures for tumor lysis syndrome is also necessary.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider thromboprophylaxis in higher-risk patients** (retroperitoneal disease over 3.5 cm, stage III or poor risk) and avoid central venous devices where possible.
claims.source_text: prevention of TEE should be particularly considered in patients at higher risk, such as those with retroperitoneal involvement >3.5 cm, stage III or poor prognosis IGCCCG []. In addition, vascular access devices should be avoided whenever possible.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Relapse after first-line chemotherapy (18–20%) is still potentially curable.** Options are conventional-dose TIP (four cycles with G-CSF) or high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell support; resect all residual lesions afterwards. Late relapse beyond 2 years: early complete surgery.
claims.source_text: Approximately 18-20% of patients with advanced TGCT are refractory or relapse after first-line chemotherapy and require additional salvage therapies, with 5-year PFS rates ranging from 54 to 90% depending on IGCCCG subgroups. These patients are still potentially curable … There are two main options for salvage treatment of these patients: conventional dose chemotherapy (CDCT), and high dose chemotherapy (HDCT). … In the CDCT approach, the most commonly used salvage regimen after BEP is four cycles of TIP with GCSF support … surgery of all residual lesions after chemotherapy must be performed in all cases if technically feasible … Late relapse after first-line chemotherapy, defined as tumor recurrence more than 2 years after primary systemic treatment, represents a special situation characterized by a higher degree of resistance to chemotherapy. In these cases, early complete surgical resection is the mainstay of treatment whenever possible.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage I seminoma on surveillance:** abdomen and pelvis imaging every 6 months for 3 years, then yearly in years 4 and 5. Chest imaging is no longer routine. Include testicular self-examination and ultrasound in follow-up.
claims.source_text: for patients who opted for active surveillance, imaging of the abdomen and pelvis is recommended every 6 months for the first 3 years and then annually in years 4 and 5. … imaging of the chest is no longer routinely recommended. … Testicular ultrasound and self-examination should be included in the follow-up.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Survivors carry late risks:** second cancers, cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, hypogonadism (11–35%), neuropathy, hearing loss and tinnitus. Counsel on lifestyle and smoking cessation, and monitor blood pressure, cholesterol and testosterone.
claims.source_text: Male hypogonadism is observed in 11-35% of this population. … Secondary neoplasms, infertility, cardiovascular toxicity, metabolic syndrome, specific sequelae of chemotherapy including neurotoxicity, ototoxicity, pulmonary and renal toxicity, and psychosocial distress associating anxiety and sexual dysfunction are the major long-term toxicities in this population … Patients should be counseled on healthy lifestyle, smoking cessation, physical activity and monitoring of blood pressure, cholesterol and testosterone levels during follow-up.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Germ Cell Cancer Group (GG), Clinical and Translational Oncology (doi 10.1007/s12094-024-03532-2), 'SEOM-GG clinical guidelines for the management of germ-cell testicular cancer (2023)', published 3 July 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467073/, retrieved 2026-09-23
